critique.paragraph: This plate reads as synthesis/integration (Edge K or L) rather than folding (Edge F). The four spheres distributed around a central specimen argue for 'bringing components together,' not 'one algorithm becoming another.' The queer_morphology_specimen is visually striking but appears as a single static form, not as a lifecycle strip showing egg → larva → imago transformation. The spatial grammar is symmetric and geometric — collect four terms, assemble at center — which is classic integration logic. Edge F requires visible metamorphosis: the same substrate at multiple stages, with the fold moment legible in space or time.
strengths: The queer_morphology_specimen has organic, transformational visual character
Text 'THE EARTH OF BECOMING' signals metamorphosis linguistically
The four spheres create a clear spatial collection task
The central specimen is visually distinctive and draws the eye
weaknesses: No visible lifecycle strip — the specimen appears once, not as three stages of transformation
Spatial arrangement is symmetric/radial, not sequential/temporal as Merian's lifecycle plates are
The four spheres suggest assembly (gather terms, build formula) not folding (one principle becomes another)
Missing the algorithmic fold — no Rule 30 → Sierpinski → BFS floor transformation as the edge sketch proposes
The formula and specimen are static; folding requires visible process or stages
The map reads as 'mastery through integration' not 'transformation through folding'
next_gen_hints: Replace the single morphology specimen with three versions along a linear path — egg (simple), larva (intermediate), imago (complex) — same form family, graduated stages
Make the floor pattern fold algorithmically as you walk: Rule 30 cells near spawn, Sierpinski triangles mid-path, BFS frontier near exit
Position the four spheres along the lifecycle strip, not in symmetric corners — collect F at egg stage, E at larva, λ and φ at imago
Change platform layout from radial (integration) to linear strip (transformation) — carousel or Merian-style horizontal lifecycle band
Add visual continuity between the three stages: same color gradient, same wireframe style, but increasing complexity
Make the formula appear/transform progressively as you walk the strip, not sit complete at the center — the equation itself should fold
